units.title: Welcome to School
units.overview: In this first unit, your child learns the words for things in the classroom, some colours, and how to say their own name and age. They meet the idea that school is a happy, welcoming place. The goal is warm, confident first steps in English — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Name a thing in your classroom
Share a school skill you have
Say what you like at school
outcomes: Name common classroom objects (table, chair, book, pencil…).
Name and point to colours (red, blue, green, yellow…).
Say “My name is ___. I am ___ years old. I like ___.”
Say the names of some school actions (read, write, draw, sing).
Join in the alphabet song and a school poem.
Use short spoken and early-written English about school, colours and confident introductions.

units.title: Family Time
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns the words for family members (mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa), some breakfast and fruit words, and how to count from 1 to 10. They talk about who is in their family and how families help and have fun together. The gentle idea is that families love and help each other. The goal is warm, confident talking in English — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Use 'he' for a boy or a man
Use 'she' for a girl or a woman
Ask your family a 'Do you like?' question
Count the people in your family
Say how you help at home
outcomes: Name the people in a family (mother, father, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa, baby).
Name some breakfast foods and fruits (pancakes, cereal, milk, mango, banana, grapes).
Count from 1 to 10, and count backwards from 10 to 1.
Ask and answer simple questions: “Do you like bananas?” → “Yes, I do.” / “No, I don't.”
Say what their family does together (help, work, play, eat, talk, laugh).
Hear the short ‘a’ sound in words like cat, hat and map.

units.title: Fun and Games
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns the words for games and play — action words like bounce, roll, throw and catch. They learn the names of parts of the body, and words that say where things are (on, under, next to), and left and right. They play simple games, learn a game from another country, and listen to a funny story. Along the way they hear the short 'u' sound (sun, fun, duck). The goal is happy, active English — learning through play.
grammar: Tell what you can do at play
Show your toy and name it
Say what you are doing right now
outcomes: Name and act out ball actions (bounce, roll, throw, catch, hit).
Name parts of the body (hand, foot, ear, nose, shoulder, head…).
Say where something is (on, under, next to) and show left and right.
Ask and answer “Can you ___?” with “Yes, I can.” / “No, I can't.”
Follow simple game instructions and take turns fairly.
Hear and say words with the short ‘u’ sound (sun, fun, duck, bug).

units.title: Making Things
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns the words for shapes, colours, and clothes, and how to make things with paper shapes — like a paper quilt, a picture, or a shape animal. They talk about what people are wearing and dress up in pretend party costumes. They meet the short ‘e’ sound (hen, pen, tent) and enjoy the old story of the elves and the shoemaker. The gentle idea running through it all is that making things takes creativity and patience — and it is fun to try, try again.
grammar: Tell everyone what you are making
Say the job you dream of
outcomes: Name and point to shapes (square, circle, triangle, rectangle).
Name and point to colours (red, blue, green, yellow, silver, gold…).
Name some clothes and costumes (hat, shirt, dress, clown, king…).
Say “I’m cutting ______.” and “I’m making a ______.”
Say “I’m wearing ______.” to describe party clothes.
Hear and say words with the short ‘e’ sound (hen, pen, ten, wet).

units.title: On the Farm
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns about the farm. They name farm animals and the sounds they make, learn farm words like tractor, barn and field, and talk about what people do on a farm — feeding, planting and picking. They meet the idea that animals and plants grow (a chick from an egg, a bean from a seed), and they hear a gentle story about helping and hard work. The goal is warm, confident spoken English — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Match the animal to its sound
Say what a farm animal is doing
Put two farm jobs in order
Spot and name what you see on the farm
outcomes: Name common farm animals (cow, hen, chick, duck, sheep, goat, horse…).
Say the sound each animal makes (moo, cluck, quack, baa…).
Name farm places and things (farm, barn, field, tractor, egg, seed).
Say what people and animals are doing: “The hen is eating.”
Tell the simple life cycle of a hen (egg → chick → hen).
Join in the “Old MacDonald” song and the farm poem.

units.title: My Five Senses
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns about their five senses — seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching — and the body parts we use for each one. They learn describing words (soft, loud, sweet, cold) and start to compare things (a tree is tall, a building is taller). Most of all, they explore the world around them and learn to be curious and thankful for all the wonderful things they can sense.
grammar: Ask which sense you are using
outcomes: Name the five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch.
Point to and name the body parts we use: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands.
Say which sense goes with which body part (“I see with my eyes”).
Use describing words: soft, hard, loud, quiet, sweet, cold.
Compare two things (tall / taller; sweet / sweeter).
Join in the “Two Little Eyes” poem and “The Music Man” song.

units.title: Let's Go!
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns how we travel and get around. They meet the words for ways to travel (walk, bus, car, bicycle, boat) and learn to say how they go to school. They talk about journeys — going somewhere with the people they love, staying safe, and enjoying the trip. The goal is warm, confident English about the everyday world of going places — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Name what you see on the journey
Say what we are doing together
Tell a journey in two steps
outcomes: Name common ways to travel (walk, bus, car, bicycle, boat, train, plane).
Say how they get to school: “I go to school by ___.”
Say the action words for travel (drive, ride, fly, float, walk).
Use simple describing words for vehicles (big, little, fast, slow, and colours).
Join in the transport songs and rhymes, doing the actions.
Use short spoken and early-written English about transport, journeys and safe travel.

units.title: Wonderful Water
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns about water — where it comes from, where we find it, and all the ways we use it every day. They meet rainy and sunny weather, animals that live in water, and the big idea that water is a gift we should not waste. The goal is warm, confident English and a thankful heart for water — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Say what you use water for
Name creatures that live in water
outcomes: Say why plants, animals, and people all need water.
Name places where we find water (rain, river, sea, well).
Say how we use water: “I use water to drink / wash / cook.”
Name some animals that live in water (fish, frog, turtle, whale).
Talk about the weather: “It is rainy.” “It is sunny.”
Join in a water poem and the “Row Your Boat” song.

units.title: City Places
units.overview: In this unit, your child learns the words for places in a town — the shop, the market, the school, the hospital, the library. They learn the people who work in these places, and simple words that tell us where things are (near, far, next to). They also meet the traffic lights and learn that red means stop and green means go. The big idea is that a town is full of helpful places and kind people, and that we all help keep our town clean and safe. The goal is warm, confident English — not perfect spelling.
grammar: Say what is in your town
Say what is next to what
Match a worker to their place
Say where you go in town
Ask politely and say thank you
outcomes: Name places in a town (shop, market, school, hospital, library, park).
Name some people who help us (teacher, doctor, shopkeeper).
Say where a place is using position words (near, next to, here, there).
Say what the traffic lights mean: red means stop, green means go.
Say “I go to the ______.” and “I can see a ______.”
Join in the traffic-lights rhyme and a town song.

units.title: My First English World
units.overview: Celebrate the learner's first year of English through a supported picture-and-word portfolio, six-page mini-book, one-minute presentation and next-goal reflection.

Learner can listen and respond to a familiar story.

Learner can present the book with an adult nearby.
Learner can reflect and name one next English goal.

units.title: Welcome and Calendar
units.overview: Welcome to your first unit of Year 2 English. You will learn how to say and spell your name, introduce a partner, and say what people like using like and likes. You will learn the calendar words too: the days of the week, the months of the year and the order words we use for dates. You will hunt for English words around your home, and ask simple questions about colours and numbers. By the end you will be ready to welcome a new friend, just as Amal does in this unit's story, “Amal's First Week”.
grammar: He and She: Choose the Pronoun
He and She: Introduce a Person
Like and Likes: Choose the Form
outcomes: Say and spell your name, and ask others how to spell theirs.
Introduce yourself and a partner using simple sentences.
Say what you and other people like, using like and likes.
Name the days of the week and the months of the year.
Say and write dates (1st, 2nd, 3rd …).
Find and read English words around you.
Ask and answer questions about colours and numbers.

units.title: Good Neighbours and Jobs
units.overview: In this unit you meet the people who live and work in your neighbourhood, and you find out what their jobs are. You learn twenty-one words for helpers, for their special clothes and equipment, and for the actions they do, from the window cleaner and the bus driver to the firefighter, the nurse and the farmer. You learn to ask questions with What and Who, to count people and objects, and to say what somebody is doing right now with is or are and a verb ending in -ing. By the end you can describe a job, name the equipment that keeps a worker safe, and be a good neighbour like the children in this unit's story, The Helpers of Warta Street.

What and Who: Building Your Own Questions
Actions Happening Now: Is or Are
Actions Happening Now: Putting the Sentence Together
outcomes: Name the different people who live and work in your neighbourhood.
Describe a job and explain what the person does in it.
Ask and answer questions using What and Who.
Count people and objects, and report the number in a sentence.
Say and write what someone is doing right now, using is or are with verb+ing.
Name the special clothes and equipment used in different jobs, and say what each one protects.

units.title: Ready, Steady, Go!
units.overview: Get ready to move! In this unit you learn the names of the parts of your body, and lots of action words such as hop, jump, clap and wave. You follow movement instructions and then give commands of your own. You also learn how to stay healthy and strong by moving every day, eating good food, drinking water and sleeping well. By the end you can say what someone is doing right now, just like Amal and her friends in this unit's story, “The Big Race”.
grammar: Actions Happening Now: Report the Race
outcomes: Identify and name different parts of your body.
Understand and use action words about movement.
Follow simple movement instructions in English.
Give simple movement instructions to others.
Describe ways to stay healthy and strong.
Create and follow a simple exercise routine.
Say what someone is doing right now, using am / is / are + verb+ing.

units.title: The Big Sky
units.overview: Look up! In this unit you learn the words for everything in the big sky: the sun, the moon, the stars, the clouds and your own shadow. You find out why a shadow is long in the morning and short at midday, and why we have day and night. You collect describing words for the sky and the weather, you write true sky facts in the present simple, and you use verbs ending in -ed to tell what you saw last night. Along the way you read “The Night Amal Counted the Stars” and wonder about the world, just as Amal does.
outcomes: Name the things you can see in the sky: the sun, the moon, the stars and the clouds.
Say what a shadow is and explain how it forms when something blocks the light.
Talk about how the sky changes in the morning, at midday and in the evening.
Explain in simple words why we have day and night.
Use describing words such as long, short, high, low, bright and dark.
Use the present simple to say true facts about the sky.
Use the past simple with verbs ending in -ed to tell what you did.
Describe today's weather using the words sunny, cloudy, windy, rainy and dry.

units.title: Let's Measure
units.overview: In this unit you learn to count in tens all the way to one hundred. You name the shapes circle, square, triangle, rectangle and heart, and you spot patterns that repeat. Best of all, you learn to measure and compare: which is bigger, which is longer, which is taller and which is heavier. You measure with a ruler in centimetres and metres, ask “How many…?” and answer with There is or There are, and you sort out the number words that sound like other words. Measuring carefully helps us understand the world and be fair to everyone, just like Amal and her friends in this unit's story, “A Fair Way to Measure”.

How Many? There is and There are
How Many? Make Your Own Survey
Words That Sound the Same: Choose and Check
outcomes: Count in tens from ten to one hundred, and choose the right number word when two words sound the same.
Name and describe the shapes circle, square, triangle, rectangle and heart.
Notice, continue and describe a pattern that repeats.
Use measuring words such as long, short, tall, heavy, light, wide and narrow.
Compare two things by adding -er to a describing word and using than.
Ask “How many…?” and answer with There is or There are.
Measure length with a ruler, using centimetres and metres.

units.title: All About Bugs
units.overview: In this unit you explore the tiny world of bugs, insects and other small garden animals. You learn the names of the butterfly, cricket, ant, bee, spider and worm, and you find out what makes an animal an insect: six legs, three body parts and two antennae. You learn position words such as on, under, between and above so that you can say exactly where a creature is, and you use the simple present tense to give true facts. By the end you can describe a creature of your own, just like Amal in this unit's story, “Amal and the Little Garden Friends”.

Asking Questions with What, Where and How
Asking Questions: Interview a Bug Expert
outcomes: Name common bugs and garden animals: butterfly, cricket, ant, bee, spider and worm.
Say what makes an animal an insect: six legs, three body parts and two antennae.
Explain why a spider and a worm are not insects.
Use position words (on, under, in, between, above, in front of) to say where a bug is.
Use the simple present tense to give true facts, such as “Bees make honey.”
Ask and answer questions with What, Where and How.
Write simple descriptions of bugs and the places where they live.

units.title: The World Around Us
units.overview: In this unit you learn about the world around us — the plants, the trees, the air, and the land and water we all share. You find out how to care for planet Earth by planting, watering, picking up litter and recycling. You learn the parts of a plant and why trees keep our air clean, and you practise saying thank you for the beautiful things in nature. By the end you can make your own promise to care for the Earth, just like Amal in this unit's story, “Amal and the Little Tree”.

Name the parts of a plant and say what each part does.

units.title: Home, Sweet Home
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 8! This unit is all about homes. You will learn the names of homes for people and for animals — a house, an apartment, a hut, a tree house, a nest, a hive and a hole. You will name the rooms inside a home and the things we keep in them, and you will compare homes from around the world. You will say where things are with in, on, under, next to, between and above, use there is and there are to say what a home has, and use will to promise the jobs you will do at home. By the end you can give a tour of your own home, just like Amal does in this unit's story, “Helping Hands at Home”.

There is / There are: What My Home Has
Talking About the Future with “will”: My Promises
outcomes: Name different kinds of homes for people and animals.
Name the rooms in a home and say what people do in each one.
Name common things at home and say which room they belong in.
Compare different kinds of homes around the world.
Use prepositions of place (in, on, under, next to, between, above) to say where things are.
Use there is and there are to say what a home has.

Describe your own home in speaking and writing.

units.title: Let's Explore the City!
units.overview: This is the last unit of Year 2, and it takes you into a busy city. You learn the names of city places such as the library, the market, the shopping center and the Ferris wheel, and the words you need to get around: bus, underground, ferry, map, directions and straight ahead. At the city aquarium you meet the octopus, the penguin, the turtle and the shark, and describe them with words like amazing, clever, huge and beautiful. You say what you like and don't like, give true facts in the present simple, and talk about what you did yesterday and what you will do tomorrow, just like Amal and her brother Adam in this unit's story, “A Big Day in the City”.

Present Simple for Facts: Aquarium Fact Cards
The Past and the Future: Yesterday and Tomorrow
outcomes: Name common places in a city, such as the library, shopping center, underground and ferry.
Talk about city sounds and the things you see, such as traffic and a helicopter.
Say what you like and don't like, and agree or disagree politely.
Describe animals and places using adjectives such as amazing, clever, huge and beautiful.
Use the present simple to state facts, such as “Octopuses have eight arms.”
Talk and write about the past and the future, such as “We went to the market. Tomorrow we will ride the ferry.”
Follow and give simple directions to get around a city.

units.title: My English World: Grade 2 Capstone
units.overview: This is the last unit of Year 2, and it gathers up everything you have learned. You revise thirty words from Units 1 to 9, from name and neighbour to butterfly, hut and underground, and you work through six grammar workshops that bring back pronouns, questions, commands, comparisons, There is and There are, and the past, present and future. Then you plan, draft, revise and publish an illustrated six-page booklet called My English World, and you present it at the class showcase just as Amal does in this unit's story.

Give, receive and act on kind, specific feedback during a peer conference.
Select portfolio evidence, reflect on progress across the year and set one next English goal.

units.title: All About Me and My Family
units.overview: Welcome to your first unit of Year 3 English. In this unit you will learn how to talk about yourself and your family, and about the values that hold a family and a school together: respect, honour, and duty. You will learn how to behave well in public and in private, and how to talk about health and safety. By the end you will introduce your family, ask Wh- questions, give clear instructions, and share what matters to you, just as Amal does in this unit's story.
outcomes: Talk about the people in your family and what you do together.
Use new words like respect, honour, duty, health, and safety.
Say what is happening now, using the present continuous (“I am helping.”).
Ask Wh- questions to find out about other people.
Give clear instructions using imperatives (“Behave well.”).
Say what you like and don't like, and join ideas with and.
Explain how to behave in public and in private places.
Write simple sentences, questions, a short play, a letter, and instructions.

units.title: School and Learning
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 2! This unit is all about school and learning. You will talk about your lessons, your teacher, and the subjects you study, like mathematics and grammar. You will learn the words for the supplies you use every day, such as an eraser and your books. You will find out how to get ready for a contest, write a short report, and use the library well. Best of all, you will learn to talk about things that happened in the past — what you studied, where you went, and why you enjoyed it. By the end, you will be ready to cheer for the Grammar Champions in this unit’s story!
grammar: Using ‘from’ to Show Where Something Comes From
Present Tense for Customs and Statements
outcomes: Name the people, places, and supplies at school, using words like teacher, library, and eraser.
Talk about your school subjects, such as mathematics and grammar, and say which you prefer.
Tell about things that happened before, using the simple past tense (studied, prepared, went).
Ask past-tense questions with Did, Was, Were and Wh– words, and answer them in full sentences.
Show who owns something, using the possessive ’s (the teacher’s pen).
Give reasons using the word because, joining a main idea to its reason.
Prepare for a contest and write a short report about a topic you have chosen.

units.title: Time and Daily Life
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 3! In this unit you will learn all about time and daily life. You will name the twelve months of the year and put them in order. You will talk about your daily routine — what you do at each hour of the day. You will learn to talk about the past (what already happened), the present (what happens every day), and the future (what will happen soon). By the end, you will be able to make your own calendar, just like Amal does in this unit’s story, “The Calendar on the Wall”.

units.title: Places and Community
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 4! In this unit you will explore the places in your community and the people who help you there. You will learn to name places like the hospital, the market, the court, the college and the garden, and to talk about helpers like the doctor, the officer and the sailor. You will describe places using words like quiet and busy, give clear instructions, ask questions with do and does, and explain your ideas with the word “because”. By the end, you will be ready to write your own report about a place in your community — just like Amal does in this unit's story.

units.title: Actions and Activities
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 5, which is all about actions and activities — the things people do. You will learn thirteen action words, including build, discuss, protect and celebrate. You will talk about what you did using the past simple, explain reasons and results with because and so, order events with First, Next, Then and Finally, ask Wh- questions, and share opinions politely. The unit story, “The Wall Behind the Garden”, follows Amal, Leo and their class as they build a reading wall together.

Talk about things you did, using the past simple (built, listened, celebrated).
Explain why something happened, using because and so.
Put events in order, using First, Next, Then, Finally.
Ask questions with what, where, who, when, why and how.
Share your ideas politely, using I think and I don't think.
Read and understand a story about working together to solve a problem.

units.title: Describing People and Things
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 6. Here you learn how to describe people and things with precise words. You collect words for what somebody is like inside, such as kind, honest, friendly and careless, and words for what things are like outside, such as rough, tough, similar and alive. You compare two people with kinder and busier, you tell true stories in the past simple, and you use could to say what somebody was able to do. Along the way you read about Amal, a new girl who discovers that carrying kindness makes everybody feel welcome.

units.title: Nature and the Environment
units.overview: Unit 7 follows Amal, Nora and Teacher Yasmin from the coast to the forest and up a mountain trail. Learners meet fifteen nature words, from climate and temperature to matter, energy and planet. They use the present perfect to say what they have seen, explored and visited, ask “Have you ever…?” questions, and build describing phrases such as “a metal rock on the beach”. The unit closes with clear instructions and a short poem about caring for our planet.

Read “From Coast to Forest” and explain what the characters felt and learned.

units.title: Numbers, Shapes, and Measurement
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 8! In this unit you use English to talk about maths in real life. You count and name big numbers, all the way up to one million. You learn the words addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. You measure the size, height, weight and distance of things around you, using words like meter and centimeter. You also hunt for straight lines and repeating patterns. Maths is everywhere: in the market, in the kitchen and on the way to school. By the end you will solve a number puzzle, just like Amal and Sami do in this unit's story.

Measure the size, height, weight and distance of things around you.

units.overview: In Unit 1 you explore daily life and communication: what people do every day, and how they share their ideas. units.title: Historical Figures and Legacy
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 7 of your Year 8 English course. In this unit, you will explore the theme of Historical Figures and Legacy -- a topic that invites you to think about how individuals shape history and how their actions echo through generations. The centrepiece is an original story, "The Rebellion of Silence", which follows Jamal, a quiet but determined student at an East African boarding school in 1948, as his anonymous essays challenge an unjust ban on debate. Alongside the story, you will master the grammar of narrating the past -- Past Simple and Past Continuous, the Past Perfect, reported speech, verbs with prepositions, phrasal verbs, reflexive pronouns, time phrases and discourse markers -- and build a rich vocabulary for discussing argument, leadership, emotion and change.

units.title: Global Storytelling and Creativity
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 8 of your Year 8 English course. This unit is called Global Storytelling and Creativity, and it is one of the most exciting units you will explore this year. Throughout this unit, you will discover how stories shape the world around us, how creative people use language to inspire and persuade, and how you can develop your own storytelling skills. You will read a powerful original story called The Edge of the Infinite, which follows a young storyteller named Imani as she competes in a national youth storytelling competition in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Her journey will show you that great stories do not simply entertain people; they change lives, preserve memories, and give voice to communities that might otherwise be forgotten.

units.title: Music as Universal Language
units.overview: Welcome to Unit 9, the final unit of Year 8. This unit is called "Music as Universal Language" because you will explore how music, performance, and the creative arts bring people together across cultures, languages, and backgrounds. Music is one of the most powerful forms of human expression. It can communicate emotions that words alone cannot capture. A song can make you feel joy, sorrow, excitement, or peace without you understanding a single word of the language in which it is sung. That is why we call music a universal language: it speaks to everyone.
outcomes: Explain what it means to call music a universal language and discuss how the performing arts connect people across cultures.

units.title: My English Voice: Grade 8 Capstone
units.overview: Unit 10 gathers the whole of Grade 8 into one evidence-led capstone. You revise thirty review words drawn from Units 1 to 8, from concise, zeal and articulate to benign, disposition and clarify. Six grammar workshops bring back comparatives and superlatives, the passive voice in four tenses, the past perfect and present perfect continuous, reported speech, conditionals, and the phrasal verbs, reflexive pronouns and quantifiers that polish a final draft. Five review texts revisit the year's stories, from Whispers Beyond the Gate to The Curtain Never Lies. You then build an inquiry product for a defined audience, defend it aloud for five to six minutes and reflect on the reader, writer and speaker you have become.
